one_liner: Deprecated Cloudflare fork of zlib 1.2.8 with SSE4.2/NEON hashing and SIMD checksums; about 4x faster deflate than stock zlib.
what_it_does: A source-compatible fork of madler/zlib (header reports ZLIB_VERSION 1.2.8) that produces standard zlib/deflate/gzip streams through the usual deflateInit/deflate/inflate/compress/gz* API. Applications relink against it without code changes, as long as they do not need APIs added in zlib 1.2.9 and later. It is also published as the Rust crate cloudflare-zlib-sys (0.3.7, marked deprecated).
how_it_is_fast: Deflate hashes 4 input bytes with one hardware CRC32C instruction (_mm_crc32_u32 on SSE4.2, __crc32cw on ARMv8 CRC) instead of zlib's 3-byte rolling shift-xor hash, which gives fewer hash collisions and shorter chain walks, and longest_match compares several bytes per step using wide unaligned loads. CRC-32 uses PCLMULQDQ carry-less-multiply folding on x86 (code copied from zlib-ng) and the ARMv8 __crc32d/w/h/b instructions on aarch64. Adler-32 uses SSSE3/NEON SIMD, and inflate uses Chromium-derived SSE2/NEON chunk copies (inffast_chunk, chunkcopy); PR #23 measured 15-34% faster decompression on Silesia files from those last two.
when_to_use: Legacy C/C++ code that links zlib and needs level 6-9 deflate 3.7-4.4x faster with byte-compatible streams and no API changes (zlib-ng discussion 871: level 9 0.476 s vs 2.106 s on Silesia-small, Ryzen 9 3900X).
Rust projects already using cloudflare-zlib-sys that cannot switch yet; Cloudflare itself recommends moving to zlib-rs.
x86-64 servers with SSE4.2 or ARMv8 machines with the CRC extension, where a fixed build target is acceptable.
High-level compression (levels 6-9) where its speed matches zlib-ng's and the API surface of zlib 1.2.8 is enough.
when_not_to_use: New projects: the README marks it deprecated with no further development planned; zlib-ng (actively maintained, runtime CPU dispatch) is as fast at level 9 and faster at levels 1-6, and libdeflate is faster still for whole-buffer use.
Fast levels: at level 1 it took 0.147 s vs zlib-ng 0.078 s and libdeflate 0.076 s in the 2025 run (it keeps zlib-like ratio, 44.16%, where zlib-ng trades ratio for speed).

Portable binaries: configure aborts on x86-64 without SSE4.2 and on aarch64 without CRC ('CRC and SSE4.2 support is required') and compiles with -msse4.2 or -march=armv8-a+crc, so the build will not run on older CPUs; there is no runtime dispatch except for PCLMUL CRC.
Code that calls newer zlib APIs: the 1.2.8-based zlib.h lacks crc32_z, adler32_z, gzfread, gzfwrite, deflateGetDictionary, inflateCodesUsed and crc32_combine_gen.
Pipelines that need output identical to stock zlib (tests with golden files, reproducible archives): the different hash produces different, at level 9 about 0.5% larger, streams.

integration.form: static lib or shared lib (configure/make or CMake); also a Rust -sys crate
integration.min_toolchain: C89-style C (zlib 1.2.8 code base) built with GCC or Clang supporting -msse4.2 (x86-64) or -march=armv8-a+crc (aarch64)
integration.platforms: x86-64 with SSE4.2 (PCLMUL optional, detected at runtime for CRC-32) and aarch64 with NEON and CRC; other architectures fall back to a generic multiply-xor hash in the source, but the README and configure checks only target these two
integration.thread_safety: Same model as zlib: separate z_stream objects are independent and can run on different threads (bundled zlib README: 'All the code is thread safe'); the PCLMUL CPU check in crc32.c uses a lazily initialised static flag.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — same zlib API, ABI and stream format, but it exposes only the zlib 1.2.8 API set (no crc32_z, gzfread and other 1.2.9+ functions), requires SSE4.2/ARMv8 CRC, and its compressed bytes differ from stock zlib

gotchas: The fork reports ZLIB_VERSION 1.2.8; selected upstream security fixes were backported by hand (the 2018 sym_buf fix, the CVE-2022-37434 extra-field bound, CVE-2016-9842 in Oct 2023, NULL checks and inflate state zeroing in Feb 2026), so version checks by scanners misreport it and anything not backported stays unfixed after deprecation.
The default branch is gcc.amd64, not master; check out that branch when vendoring.
zlib-ng's maintainer notes in discussion 871 that the fork keeps the old zlib code style and lands 'mega-commits' mixing optimizations and refactoring, with no public CI, which makes auditing hard.
Compressed output is not bit-identical to madler/zlib; ratio is slightly worse at level 9 (40.696% vs 40.490%) and slightly better at level 1 (44.160% vs 44.805%).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Rarely: pick it only when you need a zlib-1.2.8-compatible library already wired into your build (for example via cloudflare-zlib-sys) and cannot move; otherwise zlib-ng gives the same level-9 speed with active maintenance and runtime dispatch, and libdeflate is faster with better ratio when whole buffers suffice.
verified_claims_summary: The zlib-ng maintainers' deflatebench runs on Silesia-small.tar measured Cloudflare zlib against stock zlib: on a Ryzen 9 3900X with GCC 13.3.0 (2025), level 9 compression took 0.476 s vs 2.106 s and decompression 0.031 s vs 0.099 s; on an i9-9900K with GCC 4.8.5 (2021), level 9 compression took 0.544 s vs 2.760 s. Compiler flags were not stated.
status_note: Deprecated by Cloudflare (no further development; recommends zlib-rs); last commits on 2026-02-25 are backported hardening fixes, and the Zlib license makes it easy to vendor if you must.
